title: Syltade krusbär (Candied Gooseberries)
description: Prepared with gooseberries, sugar, and water.
steps: Clean the berries, rinse quickly and let drain.
From the sugar and water, boil a clear syrup, which should be thick enough that a cooled sample threads between the fingers or a drop on a plate does not spread out.
Pour the hot syrup over the berries, cover them and let stand until the next day.
Strain the syrup and pour it hot over the berries again.
On the third time, boil the berries with the syrup.
Skim the jam carefully during cooking.
Shake it in the pot until it has cooled somewhat, then immediately pour into prepared jars.

title: Syltade körsbär (Candied Cherries)
description: Prepared with cherries, sugar, and water.
steps: Rinse the cherries and pit them. Rinse the pits and crush them, and save the kernels.
From the sugar and water, boil a clear syrup, thick enough that a drop on a plate does not spread out.
Add the berries, and let the jam cook slowly under constant skimming, until the berries are clear and the syrup is thick.
Just before the jam is done, add the kernels.
Shake the jam in the pot for a while so the berries fill with syrup.

title: Syltgurkor (Pickled Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, vinegar, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 3 liters water, 1 tsp. salt (15 gr.) for blanching

steps: Peel the cucumbers, cut them lengthwise in half, remove the seeds with a silver spoon, and cut the cucumber halves crosswise.
Place some cucumbers at a time in boiling salted water and let them simmer slowly until soft, which is tested with a whisk.
Remove them with a slotted spoon, lay them on linen to drain, and then lay them in alternating layers in a jar.
Cook the sugar, vinegar, and spices tied in muslin to a clear simmering syrup, which is poured hot over the cucumbers.
Cover the jar with a doubled cloth and plate.
Place the spice bag on top of the plate.
After 3 days, strain off the syrup, boil it together with the spices, and pour it cold over the cucumbers, which are carefully covered.
Proceed in this manner two more times with six-day intervals, after which the cucumbers are ready.
Bind the jar well.

title: Syltlök (Pickled Onions)
description: Prepared with onions, vinegar, and water.
steps: Place the unpeeled onions in boiling salted water, let them cook for 2 minutes, remove and place immediately in cold water.
Peel them and let them lie in salted water (2 liters water, 2 tbsp. salt) for about 6 hours.
Heat 1 liter of the vinegar, add the onions and let them cook—small onions 5 minutes, larger ones 8-10 minutes.
If using spices, cook them for a few minutes in the vinegar and strain the brine before adding the onions; however, the onions will be whiter if the spices are omitted.
Place the onions in a jar, cover with a quadruple cloth and a plate and let stand until the following day, when the vinegar is drained off.
Cook the remaining vinegar with the sugar and let it cool.
Fill the onions into glass jars, pour the cold vinegar over them and it should stand well above the onions.
Bind the jars well and store in a cool place.

title: Syltning I (Fruit Preserve I)
description: A fruit preserve made with berries and sugar.
steps: Clean the berries, rinse them quickly in a sieve and let them drain well.
Layer them alternately with the sugar in an enameled preserve pot, cover, and let stand for one day, by which time the sugar should be nearly dissolved in the fruit juice.
Let the pot stand about 10 minutes beside the heat and then move it over gentle heat.

When the preserve has come to a boil, lift the pot from the heat and shake it carefully so that the scum can be removed, then return the pot to the heat and let the preserve simmer gently until it is clear (about 20 minutes).
During this time shake the pot often and skim the preserve carefully.
Immediately ladle the preserve into warm jars rinsed with cognac, which should stand in a cool and airy room until the preserve is cold, then cover with parchment paper dipped in cognac.
Bind the jars with parchment paper as previously described.

title: Syltning I (Jam I)

steps: Clean the berries, rinse them quickly in a sieve and let them drain well.

Pour the jam immediately into warmed jars rinsed with brandy, and let them stand in a cool, airy room until the jam is cold.

title: Syltning I (Jam Method I)
description: A fruit preserve made with berries and sugar.
steps: Clean the berries, rinse quickly in a colander and let drain well.
Layer the berries and sugar alternately in an enameled jam pot, cover and let stand for one day, until the sugar is nearly dissolved in the fruit juice.
Place the pot approximately 10 minutes beside the fire and then move it over low heat.

When the jam has come to a boil, lift the pot from the heat and shake gently so that the foam can be removed, then return the pot to the heat and let the jam simmer slowly until it is clear (approximately 20 minutes).
During this time shake the pot often and skim the jam well.
Pour the jam immediately into warmed jars rinsed with brandy, which should stand in a cool and airy room until the jam is cold, then cover with a sheet of parchment paper dipped in brandy.
Bind the jars thereafter with parchment paper as previously described.
This method is used for strawberries, raspberries, cloudberries, cloudberries, red and black currants and mixed jam of raspberries, currants and blueberries.

description: Prepared with pike, cream, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 1/2 kg pike = 200 gr scraped fish meat

steps: Clean the fish, rinse well, cut into fillets and remove the skin.
Beat the fillets with a damp meat mallet so they become even, rub with salt and vinegar and let rest 1 hour.
For the forcemeat, take the pike, rinse well and dry with a fish towel. Fillet it, scrape the fish meat finely, no scales or bones must be included.
Mix the fish meat with butter and pass 3 times through a meat grinder.
Pound the mixture in a stone mortar with a wooden pestle until it is fine and cohesive.
In a bowl, mix flour, cream, eggs and seasonings. Work this mixture into the forcemeat by spoonfuls, stirring for about 1/2 hour.

Butter a smooth timbale mold holding about 1 1/2 liters well. Wrap the fish fillets in a fish towel and line the mold with them, placing them side by side with their tails around the bottom and opposite ends protruding above the edge.
Press them well so they take the shape of the mold. Cover the fillets with a layer of forcemeat about 2 cm thick.
Place the mold in regular oven heat and let stand 10-15 minutes or until the forcemeat has set to the fillets.
Cut off the protruding fillet pieces and fill the timbale with the stew to about 3 cm from the upper edge.
Place the cut fish pieces on top of the stew and cover the timbale with a layer of forcemeat.
Bake about 45 minutes in a water bath in regular oven heat.

After the timbale is removed from the oven, let it rest 10 minutes, then turn out onto a round dish, remove the mold and garnish the top with shrimp tails and truffle slices and around with parsley or salad.

For the stew: clean the shrimp; if using lobster, cut it into pieces. Cut mushrooms and truffles into slices and sauté in butter. Sauté the crayfish butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream and let the sauce simmer 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp, oysters and mushrooms and bring the stew to a boil, add the whisked egg yolks and season with seasonings.

title: Timbales of Poultry (Poultry Timbales)
description: Prepared with game or forcemeat or grouse or meat or salt or white pepper or butter or egg or egg yolks, chicken, and water.

ingredients.name: For game forcemeat: 2 grouse or 1 female capercaillie = about 225 gr scraped meat, salt, white pepper, 100 gr panada, 100 gr butter, 1 egg, 2 egg yolks

steps: Prepare the panada: bring the water to a boil with salt and butter, then add the flour. Stir the mixture with a spoon over direct heat until it releases from the pan and spoon, then spread it on a buttered dish and brush lightly with butter on top so it does not dry out.

Place it in a bowl, add the egg together with the yolks under continuous, vigorous stirring. Pass the forcemeat through a sieve and stir again for about 1/2 hour.
Test it by cooking a small amount in salted water. If the forcemeat is too loose, add a little egg white; otherwise add an egg yolk or a little softened butter.
Butter small timbale molds and garnish with truffle cut into beautiful figures. Finely chop the remaining truffle and mix into the forcemeat.
Fill the molds 3/4 with forcemeat, bind over with butter-spread parchment paper and bake in a water bath in the oven about 45 minutes.

title: Torkning av grönsaker (Drying Vegetables)
description: Prepared with peas, beans, and spinach.

ingredients.name: Lightly salted water (1 tablespoon salt per liter of water)

steps: Drying of vegetables can be done either with or without prior blanching. It is best to blanch them. Sugar peas, fresh beans, spinach, and parsley are rinsed well, drained, and blanched for a few minutes. Rinse the vegetables with cold water, then spread them out on clean linen, preferably on drying racks, otherwise on trays, and place them in an oven with 35-40° heat (preferably a baking oven).

The vegetables should be stored in tin cans but should not be put away until they are completely dry. They are stored in a dry place.

title: Tournedos à la Nobis (Tournedos à la Nobis)
description: Prepared with beef, asparagus, and truffle.
steps: Cut slices 1 1/2 centimeters thick from the beef fillet, lightly pound them flat, form them round, season and fry in butter or braise them.
Place the steaks in small fireproof, round molds, garnish with the asparagus tips, fried in some of the butter.
Pour the Béarnaise sauce over and place a slice of truffle on each steak.
Serve as a breakfast dish with fried potatoes, sprinkled with finely chopped parsley.

For the sauce, place the seasonings and vinegar in a sauce pan. Reduce the vinegar until one-third remains, then lift the pan from the heat and let the contents cool slightly, then whisk in the egg yolks, one at a time.
Return the pan to the heat and let the sauce simmer, then add the butter little by little while whisking. Strain the sauce through a cloth and blend with a hint of cayenne and finely chopped parsley.
Heat it in a water bath until lukewarm and serve immediately. If heated too much it will break.

title: Tryffelspäckad skinka i vin (Truffle-Larded Ham in Wine)
description: Prepared with wine, truffle, and smoked ham.

ingredients.name: 1 fresh or lightly smoked ham, approximately 5 kg

steps: If using fresh ham, rub it with a mixture of salt, sugar, white pepper and ginger and let it rest for 1 day. If using smoked ham, soak it in plenty of cold water for approximately 24 hours.
Dry the ham and place it in a pot that is not too large, just large enough to fit the ham snugly. Add wine so that it reaches the same level as the ham; if needed, add more Rhine wine.
Place the lid on the pot and seal it well with a ring of dough made from coarse rye flour and water.
Cook the ham as in the previous recipe but turn it after it has cooked for 2 hours. Shake the pot frequently so that the ham does not stick to the bottom.
Place the ham in a deep dish, pour the cooking liquid over it, and let it cool in the liquid.
Remove the skin, press a towel against the fat to remove all dissolved fat, then lard the ham densely with beautifully cut truffle strips.
Beat the egg white with a fork into a light foam, mix with mustard and sugar, and brush this mixture on the ham's fat side.
Sprinkle the crushed rusks over the top. Place the ham in a roasting pan and set it in a warm oven to achieve a beautiful brown color, which takes approximately 1/2 hour.
Place the ham on a warm plate, slice it, and arrange the slices back together so that the ham appears whole.
Garnish with stewed mushrooms, tender peas, green beans, asparagus and salad or parsley.
Strain the cooking liquid, skim it well, reduce it, taste it, add finely chopped truffle, and serve in a sauce bowl.

title: Turkisk Fårstuvning (Turkish Lamb Stew)
description: Prepared with lamb, white pepper, and onion.
steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water and cut into even, beautiful pieces, which are rubbed with a mixture of salt and pepper and browned in half the butter together with the onion.
Dilute the tomato paste and brown sauce and add to the meat, which is allowed to slowly boil for approximately 45 minutes.
Transfer to another pot, strain the sauce, skim it, dilute with broth and add.
Tie together the thyme, bay leaf, and leek and add.
Prepare the carrots, beets, and celery, cut into beautiful pieces and brown in the remaining butter together with the chopped Portuguese onion.
Add the vegetables to the meat, which is then allowed to boil with a lid for approximately 30 minutes in the oven.
Test if the meat is tender.
Rinse the rice grains first with cold and then with boiling water and allow to drain well.
Then sauté them in the butter together with onion and saffron in an iron pot.
Dilute the broth, place a butter-brushed paper over it and allow the grains to boil in the oven for approximately 20 minutes.
Mix well with the cold butter and spices and arrange in a ring on a warm serving dish.
Place the meat in the middle of the dish and pour the sauce over it.
Garnish the dish with parsley and serve very hot.
Curry can be used instead of saffron.

title: Vegetarian Lökdolmar (Vegetarian Stuffed Onion Rolls, Serves 6)
description: A bread preparation made with onions, rice, and rusks.

ingredients.name: For browning: 3 tablespoons butter (60 gr), 2 cups vegetable broth or potato water

steps: Peel the onions, place in boiling salted water and let simmer gently without a lid for about 7 minutes.
Remove the onions, carefully separate the leaves and place on linen to drain.
For the forcemeat use cold rice porridge.
Beat the eggs and mix into the porridge together with the rusks and clarified butter, then season well with salt, sugar and white pepper.
Place a teaspoon of forcemeat on each onion leaf, roll up and tie with cotton string previously dipped in hot water.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the dolmas and brown nicely, then dilute with the hot vegetable broth or potato water.
Put on the lid and let braise gently for about 30 minutes.
Place on a warm platter, cut off the string and pour the sauce over it. Serve as a breakfast dish with potato pudding or fried potatoes.
